task_definition.task_name: Back Azimuth Estimation using BazNet on STEAD

task_description.overview: Estimate seismic back azimuth angles from pre-cut three-component waveform segments using a pretrained BazNet deep neural network.
steps: Load three-component waveform data arrays from the STEAD .npz file.
Normalize each component of the waveforms (zero-mean and divide by standard deviation).
Convert the normalized NumPy array to a PyTorch tensor and transfer it to the compute device (CPU or GPU).
Run the BazNet model in evaluation mode to obtain sin and cos predictions of the back azimuth.
Compute the back azimuth in degrees by applying arctangent2 to the model outputs.
Load ground truth back azimuth values from the corresponding CSV file for comparison.
Generate a scatter plot comparing inferred back azimuth versus true back azimuth with a 1:1 reference line.

task_definition.agent_prompt:
Perform back azimuth estimation on the 3-component seismic dataset (STEAD) using `baz_network` deep learning model. Load and normalize the seismic data from {data_path} with the specific {normalize_mode} mode. The pretrained baz_network model is located at {pretrained_model_path}, and its related parameters are {model_params}. 
 (1) Run inference by feeding all-length waveform into the model to obtain a single back azimuth estimate, and save the estimated value into a CSV file. 
 (2) Load the target back azimuth from {target_path} by reading the columns `back_azimuth_deg`. 
 (3) Plot one figure showing the comparison between the predicted back azimuth estimation results and the target back azimuth. Save the result data to {result_data.save_name} with content {result_data.content}, and save the result figure to {result_figure.save_name}.
